# Viewer architecture {#sec-viewer-architecture}

The viewer is plain JavaScript with ES modules and three.js. There is no build
step and no framework. This page explains how the modules are layered, how a step
reaches the screen, and what each shader draws. The list of files is on
[Basic viewer](viewer.qmd), and the integration with the platform is on
[The viewer on Qollab](qollab.qmd).

## Layers {.unnumbered}

The modules of `source/frontend/js` fall into five layers. Imports mostly point
downwards, from the entry to the foundation.

```
  entry          main.js
                   │
  interface      controls.js   panels.js   timeline.js   viewpanel.js   camerapad.js
                   │             │            │              │              │
  data           data.js ─────── host.js ──────────────────  settings.js
                   │
  scene          scene.js ── laser.js  phonon.js  trap.js  horizontal.js
                   │          measurement.js  selection.js  environment.js
                   │
  foundation     state.js   config.js   utils.js   shaders.js   three-addons.js   demo.js
```

| Layer | Modules | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Foundation | `state`, `config`, `utils`, `shaders`, `three-addons`, `demo` | Constants, shared state, small helpers and loading. They import almost nothing. |
| Scene | `scene`, `laser`, `phonon`, `trap`, `horizontal`, `measurement`, `selection`, `environment` | Build the three.js objects and update them every frame. |
| Data | `data`, `host`, `settings` | Load a visualization, talk to Python, and keep the view options. |
| Interface | `controls`, `panels`, `timeline`, `viewpanel`, `camerapad` | The buttons, panels and the timeline strip. |
| Entry | `main` | Wires everything at start-up. |

Some imports go sideways or upwards, for example `data.js` imports `panels.js` and
`timeline.js` to refresh them when the step changes, and `scene.js` imports
`settings.js` for the palettes. The one rule that is kept strictly is that **there
are no import cycles**. The bundler of the Qollab package depends on this, because
it puts the modules in the order of their imports, and a test fails if a cycle
appears (for the timeline and for the view panel).

## Shared state {.unnumbered}

`state.js` exports one object, `state`. Every module reads and writes it, and no
state hides anywhere else. It is grouped by what it describes.

| Field | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `view` | The view options (palette, what is shown, light, motion), set by `settings.js`. |
| `data`, `stepIndex` | The loaded visualization and the current position in it. |
| `playing`, `playTimer`, `pulseMs` | The automatic play and the length of the current laser pulse. |
| `qubits` | One entry per ion: the animated vector and its target. |
| `gate` | The two-qubit gate that is running, its two ions and its time window. |
| `measure`, `intro` | The measurement animation and the start-up pulse. |
| `hovered` | The ions of the gate under the pointer in the timeline. |
| `shaders` | The shader sources, loaded once. |
| `three` | The three.js objects: renderer, scene, camera and the attributes that are updated each frame. |

## From a file to the screen {.unnumbered}

```
JSON text ─► loadData(obj) ─► buildScene(n) ─► updateStep(0)
                  │                               │
                  │                    sets targets, laser pulse, gate,
                  │                    entangled pair, panels, timeline
                  ▼
            state.data                  animate(time)  ◄── requestAnimationFrame
                                           │
                                  moves each vector toward its target,
                                  writes the instance attributes,
                                  updates the layers, renders
```

1. **`loadData`** (in `data.js`) stores the visualization, builds the scene for the
   number of qubits, builds the timeline and starts the intro.
2. **`updateStep`** (in `data.js`) runs when the step changes. It does not draw. It
   sets the *targets*: where each Bloch vector must end, which ions are the targets
   of the gate, the colour and length of the laser pulse (`laserPulseFor`), the
   window of a two-qubit gate and the pair that is entangled. It also refreshes the
   panels.
3. **`animate`** (in `scene.js`) runs on every frame. It moves each vector 18 % of
   the way to its target, writes the result into the instanced attribute of the
   spheres, writes the intensity of each laser beam, calls the update function of
   every layer, and renders.

Separating the two means a step is a change of state, and the animation is a
function of time. Playing, stepping back, jumping on the timeline and loading a
file all use the same `updateStep`.

## Coordinates {.unnumbered}

The backend uses the standard Bloch convention, with `|0⟩` at `+z`. three.js has `y`
up. The conversion happens in one place, in `animate`: the Bloch vector
`(x, y, z)` is written to the shader as `(x, z, -y)`, so `|0⟩` points up. The
chain of ions runs along `x` at `y = 0`.

## The shaders {.unnumbered}

The shaders are written in GLSL in `source/shaders/`, one pair per effect. They are
loaded by `shaders.js` (over HTTP locally, or from the host on Qollab, where they
are embedded in `main.js`).

| Pair | Mesh | What it draws |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bloch.vert` / `bloch.frag` | One `InstancedMesh`, one instance per ion | The Bloch sphere: shell, great circles, axes, the state vector and its tip, the halo of an entangled ion and the red tint of decoherence. Per-instance attributes: `instancePsi`, `instanceEntangled`, `instanceDecoherence`. |
| `laser.vert` / `laser.frag` | One instanced box per ion | A volumetric laser beam, found by ray marching inside the box. `instanceActive` is the intensity of each beam; it is `0` unless the gate of the step fires on that ion. |
| `lens.vert` / `lens.frag` | The lens of each laser head | Glass with a dark base and chromatic edges. |
| `bus.vert` / `bus.frag` | A tube between the two targets of an MS or ZZ gate | The phonon bus: two waves of different frequency that travel along the tube. |
| `rail.vert` / `rail.frag` | A thin thread along the chain | The guide rail: a faint blue line that glows amber between the two ions of a running two-qubit gate. |

The options of the *View and accessibility* panel reach the sphere shader as
uniforms (`uAxisX`, `uVecColor`, `uSphereGain`, `uVectorWidth`, `uDetail`,
`uMotion`, `uHalo`, among others). A test fails if the shader declares a uniform
that the scene does not set.

Reserved words matter in GLSL. A variable called `active` stopped the guide rail
from compiling once, and the shaders use `intensity` instead.

## Layers of the scene {.unnumbered}

Each file of the *scene* layer builds one group of objects and exposes a
`create…` function, called once, and an `update…` function, called on every frame.

| Module | Builds |
| --- | --- |
| `laser.js` | The laser heads that hang from a rail, the volumetric beams, and the colour and length of the pulse of each gate. |
| `trap.js` | The chip of the surface trap: substrate, gold pads, field rings; lights the electrodes of the target ions. |
| `phonon.js` | The phonon bus, the jiggle of the ions and the synchronized halo after a two-qubit gate. |
| `horizontal.js` | The global beam, the guide rail and the side optics, and the intro pulse. |
| `measurement.js` | The fluorescence animation: readout beam, flares of the ions in `|1⟩`, photons and state badges. |
| `selection.js` | Four arcs around the ions of the gate under the pointer in the timeline. |
| `environment.js` | The optical table, the coils, the viewport frame, the fog and the lights. |

Laser pulses depend on the gate: GPI2 lasts one base pulse (650 ms), GPI two, and
MS or ZZ three, with the entangling pair in neon orange. A virtual Z fires no laser,
because it is a change of the reference frame and not a physical operation. The
automatic play waits for the pulse to end, so a long entangling gate is not cut.

## The host {.unnumbered}

`config.js` reads `window.QVIZ_HOST` once, as `HOST`. `host.js` is the only module
that talks to Python.

```
compileQasm(text) ─► HOST.compileQasm  or  POST /api/compile
sampleStep(data, step, shots) ─► HOST.sample  or  POST /api/sample
```

With no `HOST` and no server, both functions fail with a message that the error
line shows. The full table of hooks is on
[The viewer on Qollab](qollab.qmd).

## Testing without a browser {.unnumbered}

The test suite has no browser. `test_package_qollab.py` checks the viewer through
what is generated from it.

- The package is built and inspected: the file count, the absence of `main.py`, the
  license, the libraries, and that every service of the prelude is read by the
  viewer.
- The generated `main.js` and each module are checked for syntax with
  `node --check`. These tests are skipped when `node` is not installed.
- Small pieces of JavaScript are run with `node` on their own, for example the view
  options (their profiles and their storage, with a stub of `localStorage`) and the
  function that turns a Python traceback into a readable message.
- Source checks keep the layers honest: the timeline may import only `config`,
  `state` and `utils`, and every uniform that the sphere shader declares must be
  set by the scene.

Visual changes are checked by eye, locally and on Qollab, and with headless
Chromium when a rendering problem has to be reproduced.
